bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency of the Department of the Treasury relating to the review of applications under the Bank Merger Act.
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-19.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects the regulatory process banks must follow when seeking approval to merge with other banks.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn a September 2024 rule from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency that changed how bank merger applications are reviewed. The rule eliminated automatic approvals for certain mergers and ended the use of simplified application forms. If this resolution passes, those procedural changes would be nullified and the prior review process would remain in effect.

bill.title: A joint resolution disapproving the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to "Overdraft Lending: Very Large Financial Institutions".
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-10.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects overdraft fee revenue and regulatory compliance obligations at very large financial institutions.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule that limits overdraft fees at very large banks. The rule, published in December 2024, requires these institutions to either cap overdraft charges at $5, set a higher justified amount, or treat overdrafts as credit subject to Truth in Lending Act disclosures. If enacted, the resolution would prevent the rule from taking effect, leaving existing overdraft fee practices in place.

bill.title: Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-82.
subjects: War crimes, genocide, crimes against humanity

industries.rationale: The bill creates new procedural pathways and limits defenses in civil litigation, expanding the scope and duration of claims that law firms may pursue or defend.
Museums and cultural institutions that hold or exhibit artwork are directly affected by expanded liability and procedural rules for restitution claims.
Banks and auction houses that handle art transactions or hold art as collateral face potential claims if works in their possession are subject to restitution.

bill.plainSummary: This bill removes the 2026 deadline for filing lawsuits to recover art and other property taken during Nazi persecution between 1933 and 1945. It makes it easier to sue foreign governments and defendants located anywhere in the United States, and it blocks certain legal defenses that courts have used to dismiss these claims, such as arguments that too much time has passed. The changes apply to cases already filed as well as future ones.

plain.whoItTouches: People who have been the victim of a crime.

bill.title: ABC Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: Streamlined administrative processes for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP may affect how providers interact with patients' caregivers and handle eligibility documentation.
Changes to Medicare and Medicaid administrative processes could affect insurers participating in these programs and their coordination with caregivers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs federal agencies to review and simplify the paperwork and application processes for Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Social Security. The goal is to reduce the burden on family caregivers by eliminating duplicative forms and streamlining eligibility procedures across these programs. Agencies must gather input from caregivers and state organizations, make improvements, and report their progress to Congress.

bill.title: FIND Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly protects firearm manufacturers, dealers, and trade associations from discrimination in federal contracting.
Banks and financial institutions that provide services to federal contractors would be affected if they maintain policies restricting business with firearm entities.
Defense contractors frequently hold federal contracts and may need to review policies regarding firearm-related business relationships.
Insurance companies that contract with the federal government would need to ensure their underwriting policies do not discriminate against firearm businesses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit federal agencies from awarding contracts to companies that discriminate against firearm manufacturers, dealers, or trade associations. Contractors would be required to certify they have no policies that discriminate against firearm-related businesses and will not adopt such policies during the contract term. The requirement would apply to both prime contractors and subcontractors, with penalties for violations, but would not apply to sole-source contracts.

bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.

The rule was designed to improve tax compliance by ensuring the IRS receives information about cryptocurrency sales, similar to reporting requirements for stocks and other securities. If passed, the resolution would nullify this reporting requirement before it takes effect.

bill.title: A resolution recognizing community care as an essential tool for meeting the health care needs of the veterans of the United States.
bill.latestActionText: Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S8874; text: CR S8874)

industries.rationale: The resolution emphasizes community care, which directs veterans to private hospitals and physician groups when VA facilities cannot meet demand.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution is a non-binding statement recognizing that community care—health services provided by private providers outside the VA system—is an important way to meet veterans' health needs. It urges the Department of Veterans Affairs to fully implement the 2018 law that created the Veterans Community Care Program, ensuring veterans can access private providers when the VA cannot serve them in a timely manner. The resolution does not change law or create new programs; it expresses the Senate's support for existing community-care arrangements.

plain.whoItTouches: Veterans and their families.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: Justice for Victims of Sanctuary Cities Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: State and local governments face new legal liability and compliance obligations regarding federal immigration detention requests.
The bill creates a new private right of action and liability framework, directly affecting litigation practice and municipal legal defense work.
Municipal liability insurers would face new exposure from lawsuits against local governments under the bill's provisions.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow victims of certain felonies committed by non-citizens to sue state or local governments that did not comply with federal immigration detention requests. Jurisdictions that accept certain federal grants could not claim immunity from such lawsuits. The bill also provides legal protections to jurisdictions and their employees who do comply with federal immigration detention requests.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-26.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

bill.title: EASE Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: The bill directly establishes a payment model for federally qualified health centers, rural health clinics, critical access hospitals, and rural emergency hospitals to furnish specialty care services.
The bill requires digital methods and telehealth technology to deliver remote specialty care, creating demand for broadband and telecommunications infrastructure in rural areas.
The bill's reliance on telehealth platforms and digital coordination systems would affect vendors providing health IT and telemedicine software solutions.
The bill modifies service delivery and reimbursement models for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP, which may affect how insurers and managed-care organizations structure networks and payments.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to test a program that uses networks of rural health providers to deliver specialty medical care remotely to Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP patients in rural areas. The networks must include at least 50 qualifying rural clinics or hospitals, be nonprofit, and use telehealth technology to connect patients with specialists while coordinating with their primary care doctors. At least half of the providers in each network must be located in rural areas.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-1.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

bill.title: Family Farm and Small Business Exemption Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly exempts family farms from asset calculations for federal student aid eligibility.
The bill changes how federal student aid eligibility is calculated, affecting aid distribution and potentially enrollment patterns.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restore an exemption that allows families to exclude the value of their farm or small business (with 100 or fewer employees) when applying for federal student aid. Recent changes to the financial aid application began counting these assets when determining how much aid a student qualifies for, starting in the 2024-2025 school year. The bill would return to the previous policy of not counting these family-owned farms and businesses as assets in the aid calculation.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, and people paying off a student loan. Students, and their families.

bill.title: Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects manufacturers and sellers of lead ammunition by limiting federal authority to regulate their products on public lands.
Manufacturers of fishing tackle containing lead would face fewer potential federal restrictions on their products' use.
Sporting goods retailers selling lead ammunition and tackle would benefit from reduced regulatory uncertainty around these product lines.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent three federal agencies—the Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Forest Service—from banning or regulating the use of lead ammunition or fishing tackle on federal lands and waters. The agencies could still impose restrictions in specific locations if they determine, based on field data from that site, that lead use is the primary cause of a wildlife population decline and the state agrees to the regulation. Certain existing regulations would remain in place.

districtAwards.recipientName: NORTH CAROLINA DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL AND CULTURAL RESOURCES
districtAwards.description:
DESCRIPTION:THIS ACTION APPROVES AN AWARD IN THE AMOUNT OF $421,238,074 TO PROVIDE FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO THE NORTH CAROLINA DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL AND CULTURAL RESOURCES. THE RECIPIENT WILL IMPLEMENT GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) REDUCTION PROGRAMS, POLICIES, PROJECTS, AND MEASURES IDENTIFIED IN A PRIORITY CLIMATE ACTION PLAN (PCAP) DEVELOPED UNDER A CLIMATE POLLUTION REDUCTION GRANTS (CPRG) PLANNING GRANT.ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES TO BE COMPLETED DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD ARE DESCRIBED IN 21 PROJECTS UNDER TWO MEASURES. MEASURE 1 OF THIS PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON PROTECTING AND RESTORING HIGH-CARBON COASTAL HABITATS AND PEATLANDS TO MAXIMIZE CARBON SEQUESTRATION AND COASTAL RESILIENCE BENEFITS.  NINE ACTIVITIES WILL FALL UNDER THIS MEASURE. MEASURE 2 OF THIS PROPOSAL ADDRESSES THE PROTECTION, USE, AND RESTORATION OF FORESTED LAND, PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE FORESTRY MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO INCREASE CARBON SEQUESTRATION.  TWELVE ACTIVITIES WILL FALL UNDER THIS MEASURE. SUBRECIPIENT:NCCF - IMPLEMENT COASTAL HABITAT AND PEATLAND PROTECTION, RESTORE PROJECTS, CONDUCT MONITORING AND SCIENTIFIC ANALYSIS, REPORT RESULTS; MARYLAND DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (MDNR) - PROJECT MANAGEMENT, LANDOWNER OUTREACH, PROJECT SELECTION, SUBCONTRACTING, VERIFICATION, AND TRACKING REPORTING METRICS.;VA DEQ - LEAD AGENCY TO ADMINISTER AND DISBURSE FUNDS AS SUBAWARDS TO PARTNERS AND MANAGE ALL PROJECTS REPORTING TO NC DNR.;VA DEPARTMENT OF WILDLIFE RESOURCES (DWR) - WILL IMPLEMENT PROJECTS 1-7 WITH PARTNERS, HANDLE COASTAL SHORELINE, MARSHLAND, PEATLAND PROTECTION AND RESTORATION PROJECTS, LAND ACQUISITION, MONITORING AND ANALYSIS, HIRING, REPORTING.;VPA -  RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING PROJECT 8. THIS ENTAILS WORKING WITH PARTNERS TO PURCHASE A CONSERVATION EASEMENT AND PERFORM REFORESTATION ACTIVITIES.;TNC - ACQUIRING INTERESTS IN PROPERTY, RESTORING ECOLOGICAL FUNCTION, AND INCREASING CARBON RETENTION/ SEQUESTRATION RATES.;NC FOREST SERVICE - CREATE A RAPID GROWTH FOREST DEVELOPMENT COST SHARE PROGRAM AND AN URBAN TREE PLANTING GRANT PROGRAM FOR MUNICIPALITIES AND NON-PROFITS TO APPLY.;SUSTAINABLE FORESTRY AND LAND RETENTION PROJECT - EXPAND CURRENT GEOGRAPHICAL AREA TO REACH ADDITIONAL LIDACS AND PROVIDE ACCESS TO TECHNICAL AND FINANCIAL RESOURCES; BLACK FAMILY LAND TRUST (BFLT) - ACQUIRE CONSERVATION EASEMENTS ON LAND IN LIDACS; IN PARTNERSHIP WITH ROANOKE SFLRP IMPLEMENT A COST SHARE PROGRAM TO IMPLEMENT CLIMATE SMART REFORESTATION/FORESTRY PRACTICES;SCOR - IDENTIFY AND ACQUIRE LAND FOR CONSERVATION, MEASURE AND MONITOR CARBON BENEFITS AND CO-BENEFITS. IT IS SCOR'S RESPONSIBILITY TO DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, AND MAINTAIN THE STATEWIDE RESILIENCE PLAN;MD DEPT. OF NATURAL RESOURCES - PROJECT MANAGEMENT, LANDOWNER OUTREACH, PROJECT SELECTION, SUBCONTRACTING FOR IMPLEMENTATION, VERIFICATION AND TRACKING PROJECT SUCCESS, REPORTING METRICS; MD DEPT. OF AGRICULTURE - PROJECT MANAGEMENT, LANDOWNER OUTREACH, PROJECT SELECTION, SUBCONTRACTING FOR IMPLEMENTATION, VERIFICATION AND TRACKING PROJECT SUCCESS, REPORTING METRICS; AND MD DEPARTMENT OF THE ENVIRONMENT (MDE) - PROJECT MANAGEMENT, INTER-AGENCY COORDINATION, INTER-AGENCY PROJECT TRACKING IMPLEMENTATION.




OUTCOMES:THE ANTICIPATED DELIVERABLES FOR MEASURE 1 AND 2 INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: 33,000 ACRES OF PEATLANDS NEWLY PRESERVED AND/OR RESTORED IN NC AND VA (TNC), 150 ACRES OF TIDAL WETLANDS RESTORED IN VA (TNC), 15 ACRES OF PEATLANDS AND 595 ACRES OF COASTAL HABITATS NEWLY PRESERVED AND RESTORED (NC), 3,300 ACRES PERMANENTLY ADDED TO STATE PARK SYSTEM (NC),10,000 OF ACRES OF FORESTS, CURRENT OR FUTURE COASTAL HABITATS, OR AGRICULTURAL LANDS RESTORED (MD), 1,540 ACRES OF COASTAL HABITATS RESTORED (MD). 67,647 ACRES OF FORESTS UNDER IMPROVED MANAGEMENT IN THE APPALACHIANS IN MD AND VA (TNC), 25,447 ACRES OF BOTTOMLAND HARDWOOD FOREST UNDER IMPROVED MANAGEMENT IN SC AND VA (TNC), AT LEAST 55,000 ACRES OF LAND REFORESTED (NC), APPROXIMATELY 12,240 ACRES PLACED INTO CONSERVATION, WITH
